prose.def: To listen attentively, taking someone's words into your ears and giving them your full attention.
prose.article: ἐνωτίζομαι literally means to "take into one's ear" — to give ear to something and listen carefully. It appears just once in the New Testament, in Acts 2:14, where the Majority Standard Bible renders it "carefully" (and the Berean Standard Bible agrees 100%). It is far more common in the Septuagint, where it shows up 33 times across 11 books, most often translating the Hebrew הֶאֱזִין ("give ear") 19 times; one interesting debate is whether the Greek translators coined the word to mimic this Hebrew expression or simply borrowed it from everyday speech, where Moulton-Milligan finds it attested in ordinary Koine papyri.

prose.def: To take something out, whether literally gouging out a body part or figuratively rescuing someone from danger.

prose.def: A conjunction meaning "when" or "as soon as," marking the time at which something happens once a condition is met.

prose.def: A conjunction meaning "since indeed" or "seeing that," introducing a reason or cause.
prose.article: ἐπείπερ is a causal conjunction built from ἐπεί ("since") plus the emphasizing particle περ, giving the sense "since indeed" or "seeing that." It is exceptionally rare, appearing in only 1 place in the Byzantine New Testament (Romans 3:30) and not at all in the critical (SBLGNT) text. The everyday Koine papyri show its ordinary use well: a 165 B.C. document reads "since (ἐπείπερ) it is necessary to keep reminding you continuously about the same things."
prose.caution: The reading is disputed — Abbott-Smith notes that while the Received Text has ἐπείπερ at Romans 3:30, Westcott and Hort read εἴπερ instead, and the critical text omits it entirely.

prose.def: The bringing in of something additional or in place of what came before.
prose.article: ἐπεισαγωγή describes the act of introducing something extra or in addition to what already exists. prose.def: A linking adverb meaning "then" or "afterward," marking the next item in a sequence of events or a list.
prose.article: ἔπειτα is a sequencing word that points to what comes next, whether in time ("afterward") or in an ordered list ("then, second..."). The Byzantine NT uses it 16 times, and in 10 of those it gets absorbed into the English phrasing without a word of its own, which tells you it mainly oils the joints of a sentence rather than carrying weight by itself. It often teams up with "first" (πρῶτον...ἔπειτα), and the everyday papyri show the same pattern—one writer opens "first greeting you, then praying to all the gods."
prose.caution: Septuagint evidence is very thin (just one occurrence), but the NT and papyri usage agree closely.

prose.def: An adverb meaning "beyond" or "on the far side of," pointing to something past a stated place.
prose.article: ἐπέκεινα is a spatial adverb meaning "beyond" or "on the further side of," typically used with a genitive to mark what lies past a given point.
